nodes.label: AMPM Platform — Your Brief, Annotated
nodes.rationale: Hands AMPM's five documents back reproduced in full, with every audit finding placed at the passage it concerns in six callout kinds (gap, conflict, ambiguity, decision, assumed, covered), so the review happens in context rather than against a separate findings list.

nodes.label: Open decisions document
nodes.rationale: Lists all 25 decisions (Q1-Q25) with the choices AMPM can make.

nodes.label: Assumptions sheet
nodes.rationale: Lists every placeholder assumption (A/U/W/T/P tags) taken so that design could continue while AMPM decides.

nodes.label: Requirements audit
nodes.rationale: Found 9 conflicts, 44 gaps, 15 ambiguities and 25 decisions across AMPM's five documents.

nodes.label: Data model (106 tables)
nodes.rationale: Extends the specification's 35-table suggested model to 106 tables so every record named in the module inventory has a table (GP-16), keeping every original table name.

nodes.label: Permission matrix
nodes.rationale: Has a table for every account state (GP-1), names who may make every status change (GP-19), and defines ten visibility classes with named readers and writers.

nodes.label: Field matrix (1,068 fields)
nodes.rationale: Generated from the data model so the two cannot drift; states for every field the stage at which it becomes required, so a wedding project needs only four fields to exist.

nodes.label: Wireframe specification (124 screens)
nodes.rationale: 124 screens, 67 for the team workspace alone, with a table mapping every item in the brief's main-screens list to its screen; the redrawn flowcharts are the structure to approve.

nodes.label: User flows
nodes.rationale: Twelve numbered flows (demo and subscription, hotel assistance, project creation, requests, RSVP, live operations, closure, expiry) that the redrawn flowcharts point to.

nodes.label: Architecture plan
nodes.rationale: Holds the six purely technical gaps (sizing, performance targets, security hardening, delivery pipeline, GST compliance detail, hosting location); every notification and automation rule is a job or event handler in it.

nodes.label: Test cases (208 tests, 36 acceptance criteria)
nodes.rationale: The fifteen acceptance scenarios have five to ten tests each, 208 in total; twenty-one further criteria were derived from the non-functional requirements; each phase has a named test pack that must pass before it closes.

nodes.label: AMPM Website & App — Simple Business Explanation for Developer
nodes.rationale: The client's plain-language brief: four parts of the platform, a ten-step business process, the information to manage, nine development rules, the main screens, what the developer should do first and the decisions that must not be assumed.

nodes.label: Why AMPM App note
nodes.rationale: Positions AMPM as a paid, client-based platform rather than a public app: four stages (see, demo, subscribe, full project), three environments, a private hotel database and access-control rules including no self-registration.

nodes.label: AMPM Developer Technical Specification v1.0 (20 October 2026)
nodes.rationale: Treated as the authoritative requirements document and extended rather than replaced: every table name in its data model is kept. Its roles, statuses and phases are treated as proposals because it carries no sign-off and the brief says roles and release scope must not be assumed.

nodes.label: Cost estimate and milestone schedule (held)
nodes.rationale: Held until Q1 (delivery platform) and Q15 (volumes) are answered, because platform choice and volumes change the estimate more than anything else; the phases themselves are drafted.

nodes.label: GAP finding (GP)
nodes.rationale: Something the platform needs that no document specifies; each names its audit identifier and says how the design fills it meanwhile. 44 in the audit, 38 placed in the brief, 6 purely technical ones in the architecture plan.

nodes.label: CONFLICT finding (CF)
nodes.rationale: Two of AMPM's documents say different things; AMPM chooses which stands. All nine are placed in the brief.

nodes.label: AMBIGUITY finding (AM)
nodes.rationale: A sentence that can be read two ways; the brief says which reading was taken. 15 in the audit, 9 placed; the other six are modelling detail answered in the data model.

nodes.label: DECISION question (Q)
nodes.rationale: A question only AMPM can answer; all 25 are placed in the brief and listed with choices in the open decisions document.

nodes.label: ASSUMED placeholder (A/U/W/T/P)
nodes.rationale: What was done in the meantime, with its identifier. No price, fee or term is in code; every open policy is a tagged assumption so that design could continue.

nodes.label: COVERED requirement
nodes.rationale: A requirement the design meets as written, marked so AMPM can see what needs no discussion.

nodes.label: Public website
nodes.rationale: Shows only hotels flagged for showcase, and only their name, destination and a photo; never reads the private hotel database.

nodes.label: Client portal
nodes.rationale: Hotel discovery for subscribers and a wedding workspace for engaged clients; clients see only information intended for them, enforced on the server.

nodes.label: AMPM team workspace
nodes.rationale: Internal system for enquiries, hotels, projects, vendors, budgets, guests, tasks and execution; internal notes, negotiations and margins never leave the server for a client session.

nodes.label: Guest RSVP portal
nodes.rationale: Guests confirm attendance and give travel and accommodation details through a private link; team manual entry writes the same records so a phone call never creates a duplicate.

nodes.label: Demo / trial mode
nodes.rationale: The Why note requires a distinct demo environment that the specification mentions only as one screen and one test and assigns to no phase (CF-1, GP-2). Placed in Phase 1 as a mode of one platform: Sales grants it from the lead record, it is time-boxed, shows a curated set of hotels with prices hidden plus one sample wedding, and every query for a demo user is limited to flagged records (U-1, A-10, A-28). A separately hosted demo is possible at extra cost.

nodes.label: Three distinct environments (public website, demo/trial, private platform)
nodes.rationale: CF-9/AM-8: could mean three separately hosted systems or three experiences of one; the specification asks for one shared backend, so one platform was built with flagged demo accounts and demo weddings.

nodes.label: Private hotel database
nodes.rationale: A private AMPM resource, not a public directory: public visitors see selected examples, prospects see sample or limited data, subscribers see the module their plan includes.

nodes.label: AMPM business process (Steps 1-10)
nodes.rationale: Enquiry, introduction and demo, optional subscription, hotel exploration, optional hotel services, project creation if hired, parallel activities, vendor options, execution, closure.

nodes.label: Customer journey stages 1-5 (website, demo, subscription, project, full access)
nodes.rationale: Seeing AMPM, trying a demo, buying a subscription and receiving full project access are four different stages; the design has a client account state for each.

nodes.label: Critical rule: hotel-discovery subscription never implies full wedding management
nodes.rationale: A subscription grants only hotel modules; wedding modules come only from a service agreement and project membership. Subscription and service agreement are two separate records so the service stages stay distinct but connected.

nodes.label: Client vs internal visibility rule (server-side enforcement)
nodes.rationale: Internal cost, margin, private notes and identity references must be protected by strict server-side field permissions; hiding frontend controls is not sufficient. The rule the whole permission design is built on.

nodes.label: Module inventory (14 modules)
nodes.rationale: GP-16: twenty-five records named here (plan, inventory snapshot, negotiation, site visit, quote, change request, family group, readiness check, final account and more) had no table in the suggested data model; all are modelled now.

nodes.label: Suggested relational data model (35 tables)
nodes.rationale: The specification's logical model; kept in full and extended with rate cards, plans, room blocks, payment directions, GST fields, media rights and household records.

nodes.label: Field specification pattern
nodes.rationale: For every field: name, type, options, who edits, visibility, requiredness by stage, automation and report impact; avoid making all fields mandatory at project creation.

nodes.label: Notification and automation rules
nodes.rationale: Payment activates only the purchased entitlement; stale pricing is flagged; approvals notify decision-makers; material changes flag budgets and run-of-show; RSVP changes recalculate attendance and flag menu, room and transport impacts. Each rule is a job or an event handler in the architecture, each with a test.

nodes.label: Reports and exports respecting permissions
nodes.rationale: Every report lists who may run and export it; exports strip sensitive, identity and bank data always and internal cost unless the exporter is Finance.

nodes.label: Technical and non-functional requirements
nodes.rationale: Responsive interface, shared backend, server-side authorisation, encryption, private file storage, audit trail, backups, bulk operations, configurable commercial rules, retention rules, documented integration boundaries.

nodes.label: Five implementation phases (foundation, planning, guest operations, live execution, stabilisation)
nodes.rationale: Demo and trial placed in Phase 1 (A-10); Phase 1 assumed to include the full hotel-assistance workflow, online payment and website editing (Q10); invitation design in Phase 2 and sending in Phase 3 (AM-12); each phase has a named test pack.

nodes.label: Fifteen acceptance test scenarios
nodes.rationale: Enquiry capture, subscription scope, demo isolation, price freshness, negotiation privacy, project permissions, independent functions, vendor shortlist size, version-locked approvals, duplicate-free RSVP, attendance impacts, URL/API/file access control, readiness gate, incidents, closure checks.

nodes.label: Decisions AMPM must confirm (specification §13)
nodes.rationale: The ten listed map to Q3, Q4, Q5, Q4, Q9, Q11, Q8, Q16, Q14 and Q10; the audit found eight more that block design just as much: Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7, Q13, Q12, Q14 and offline use (Q1).

nodes.label: Eleven proposed user roles (P-1)
nodes.rationale: CF-7: the specification lists Super Admin, Sales, Hotel team, Project Manager, Creative, Vendor Coordinator, RSVP team, Hospitality, Finance, Client decision-maker and Guest as if final while the brief says roles must not be assumed; treated as AMPM's proposal to confirm (Q6).

nodes.label: Sample Jaipur wedding (four functions, 412 guests)
nodes.rationale: The brief's worked example (250 guests in Jaipur) is the sample wedding used throughout the drafts and the test data, so every screen and test is checked against the case AMPM described.

nodes.label: Client account states (subscriber-only, engaged, expired, closed)
nodes.rationale: GP-1: three sources of access (subscription, agreement, project) were named without saying how they combine. The permission matrix has a table per state: an expired subscriber keeps saved-hotel names and read access to enquiries, an engaged client keeps the wedding workspace whatever the subscription does, and expiry never deletes anything.

nodes.label: Subscription purchase path: request on website, AMPM invites, client pays in portal, modules activate
nodes.rationale: CF-5: the Why note says AMPM creates every account and nobody registers, the specification describes a website payment journey. Reconciled: the client requests access on the website, AMPM creates the account and invites them, the client pays inside the portal online or by bank transfer (U-2, W-15). No registration route exists, with a test.

nodes.label: Subscription plans with included modules
nodes.rationale: GP-3: subscriptions.plan_id pointed at a plan table that did not exist; plans and their included modules were added, editable by AMPM without code.

nodes.label: One-time fixed-term subscription (assumed)
nodes.rationale: GP-4: recurring billing is a sizeable feature and nothing says the subscription recurs; assumed one-time for a fixed term (A-3) pending Q3.

nodes.label: Service agreement for hotel assistance and wedding management
nodes.rationale: GP-5: an availability check is included in the subscription; negotiation, site visits, contract review and booking assistance wait for an agreement the team sends and the client accepts in the portal (U-3). An accepted agreement for anything beyond hotel help creates the wedding project (U-6).

nodes.label: Wedding project
nodes.rationale: U-6: created when an agreement beyond hotel help is accepted; links the account's saved hotels and enquiries automatically (GP-27); only a name, the account, tentative dates and a lead are required at creation, so nothing is re-entered and no giant mandatory form exists.

nodes.label: Parallel workflows after project creation
nodes.rationale: Vendors, design, invitations, guests, rooms and budget are independent streams once a project exists; none waits for another.

nodes.label: Rate cards per season with verified line items
nodes.rationale: GP-8: the brief requires quoted prices and verification dates but hotels and hotel_rooms/venues have no price field. Rate cards per season carry room rates, venue rental, per-plate minimums and taxes, each with a verification date (A-9).

nodes.label: Verification dates and stale labels
nodes.rationale: Every price shows Verified on with the date and team member, turns Stale after a period AMPM sets, and is never described as confirmed; verification is per field group for hotels, with verified availability windows for vendors.

nodes.label: Availability answered inside enquiries, not a live calendar
nodes.rationale: GP-9: availability had no home; assumed to be answered by the team inside each enquiry rather than kept as a live calendar (Q9).

nodes.label: Media rights status and consent record
nodes.rationale: GP-20: previous wedding photos are other clients' weddings, and documents/media had a visibility flag but no record of rights. Every photo and video carries a rights status and consent reference and cannot be shown without one.

nodes.label: Saved hotels and hotel compare
nodes.rationale: GP-10: save favourites had no record; one was added together with compare, and saved hotels attach to the project on creation.

nodes.label: Private RSVP link per household
nodes.rationale: AM-1: one shared link would force guests to find themselves in a list and let them see other families. A private link per household means the guest list must exist before invitations go out (A-7, Q7).

nodes.label: Person as counting unit, household as grouping
nodes.rationale: GP-13: counting by family or by person was left open; guest_function_attendance was per guest yet carried a party_count. The person is the unit and the household the grouping so children, rooms and meals are counted correctly.

nodes.label: Meal preference collected, allergies optional and restricted
nodes.rationale: GP-24: menus and caterers need meal preferences, which no document mentions; medical data is named only in the reports section.

nodes.label: Identity document capture: per wedding only, Aadhaar refused, locked store, deleted 30 days after checkout
nodes.rationale: GP-41: Indian rules restrict storing Aadhaar numbers, and the specification says identity documents must never be universally required. Switched on per wedding only, Aadhaar refused outright, files kept in a separate locked store seen only by named staff and deleted thirty days after checkout (A-8, Q8).

nodes.label: Digital Personal Data Protection Act
nodes.rationale: GP-40: applies to every guest, who has no contract with AMPM; consent capture, retention and a breach procedure are designed in, and the enquiry form must ask consent in wording AMPM approves (Q17).

nodes.label: Ten visibility classes enforced server-side
nodes.rationale: Ten visibility classes, each with named readers and writers; a client-facing response is built from a separate model that simply does not contain internal fields, with tests that no restricted field ever appears in a client response.

nodes.label: Separate client-facing amount and internal cost on every money record
nodes.rationale: Every money record has a client-facing amount and a separate internal cost (vendor_proposals.client_visible_amount vs internal_cost) so margins never leave the server for a client session.

nodes.label: Designed for the margin model, also works for a visible-fee model
nodes.rationale: Q4/A-4: if AMPM earns a margin on vendor prices the client must never see cost; if it charges a visible fee they may. Designing for the margin case also serves the fee case.

nodes.label: Three client roles with a separate finance flag
nodes.rationale: GP-26: 'clients' means the couple, paying parents and a helping sibling; one client role cannot express them. Three client roles plus a separate switch for who may see money (A-5, Q5).

nodes.label: Statuses and transition permissions for every record kind
nodes.rationale: GP-19: the specification had statuses for ten record kinds and none for twelve others (vendor assignment, vendor proposal, design version, menu version, invitation, guest response, payment, invoice, contract, service agreement, travel, guest request) and said nothing about who may move a record between statuses; all defined, with the permission matrix naming who may make each change. A trial status was added to Subscription (GP-2).

nodes.label: Append-only audit of a fixed list of actions
nodes.rationale: Important budget, approval, payment and contract changes record who and when, with before and after values.

nodes.label: Offline-readable cue sheet, readiness checks and arrival lists
nodes.rationale: GP-34: wedding-day execution happens on phones inside venues with poor signal and no document mentions offline. Cue sheet, readiness checks and arrival lists are readable offline with updates queued until signal returns (T-11, Q1).

nodes.label: Staff rosters per function
nodes.rationale: GP-30: execution needs to know who is on site and when.

nodes.label: Closure checklist verified against the data
nodes.rationale: Every guest departed, nothing left in lost and found, every vendor confirmed complete, final accounts approved by Finance.

nodes.label: Twelve-month read-only client access after closure, then archive
nodes.rationale: A-23: after closure the couple keeps read-only access for twelve months, then the wedding is archived; nothing is deleted (Q23, Q24).

nodes.label: Feedback form and archived state at closure
nodes.rationale: GP-29: feedback and archive appear only in the team-app flowchart and had no records (A-24).

nodes.label: Tracked change request
nodes.rationale: GP-14: named in the module inventory and the client-portal flowchart but with no record, statuses or rules. Tracked from submitted to implemented; an accepted change to an approved item produces a new version for a new approval (A-21, Q21).

nodes.label: Approvals locked to the exact version
nodes.rationale: An approval refers to the exact design, menu or proposal version; revisions do not overwrite it and a superseded version keeps its decision.

nodes.label: Several hotels and venues outside the database per wedding
nodes.rationale: GP-12/AM-2: wedding_projects.hotel_id allowed one hotel; destination weddings use a main hotel plus overflow hotels, and functions may be at venues outside the database (A-18, Q18).

nodes.label: Room blocks held per hotel, category and dates
nodes.rationale: GP-11: rooms were allocated with nothing to allocate them from; blocks let allocations be checked against what is actually held (Q19).

nodes.label: Payment and invoice direction
nodes.rationale: GP-17: payments had no direction so a client's payment and a payment to a vendor looked alike, and contracts/invoices had one amount that would show a vendor's invoice to a client; vendor-side records are never client-visible.

nodes.label: GST fields on invoices
nodes.rationale: GP-18: no tax fields existed (Q16).

nodes.label: Payment milestones with due dates and a refund path through the gateway
nodes.rationale: GP-6/GP-7: payment stages for wedding management and refund handling had no records or rules; designed with the amounts and terms left to AMPM (Q3, Q4).

nodes.label: Vendor availability with verification date
nodes.rationale: GP-21: listed in the brief but had no record.

nodes.label: Vendors and hotels do not log in (vendor portal deferred)
nodes.rationale: Q22/A-22: nothing says whether vendors or hotels log in; assumed not in this project, and a vendor portal can be added later without changing the vendor records.

nodes.label: Five to ten vendor options as a guideline, not a rule
nodes.rationale: Two options present cleanly and twelve are not blocked; clients see the vendor's name, description and portfolio, never contacts, raw quotes or internal ratings.

nodes.label: Notification channels (in-app, email, WhatsApp, SMS) with per-person preferences
nodes.rationale: GP-32: notifications had no channels or preferences defined; designed with a WhatsApp opt-in (A-11, Q11), and every notification logged with recipient, channel, timestamp and delivery status.

nodes.label: Material change threshold (10% budget line move, date or venue change)
nodes.rationale: AM-4: 'material changes' had no definition; assumed a budget line moving ten percent or more, or a date or venue change, with the thresholds as settings (A-25, Q25).

nodes.label: Backup targets: 15-minute data loss, 4-hour recovery, second Indian region
nodes.rationale: Q14: backups and restoration need targets for how much data may be lost and how long recovery may take; assumed fifteen minutes and four hours, with copies in a second Indian region (T-13).

nodes.label: Typed, tracked requests instead of live chat
nodes.rationale: GP-15: 'messages, questions' in the client-portal flowchart describes a chat feature no other document mentions; designed as typed, tracked requests with a conversation under each that the team answers (A-20, Q20).

nodes.label: Website content editor for pages, destinations and showcase items
nodes.rationale: GP-23: 'showcase selected work' and 'content managed by AMPM' mean someone edits the website and no document says whether AMPM or the developer does; a simple editor was designed (W-4, Q12).

nodes.label: Consultation and questionnaire as lead activities
nodes.rationale: CF-8: consultation and questionnaire appear only in the team-app flowchart; made activity types the team logs on a lead, with the questionnaire a structured form AMPM can edit (W-12).

nodes.label: Calendar of functions, visits, deadlines and shifts with a personal feed
nodes.rationale: GP-28: schedule and calendar on the Home tab appear only in the flowchart; staff can add the feed to their own calendars.

nodes.label: Spreadsheet import for hotel data and guest lists
nodes.rationale: GP-22: bulk operations are required but no import exists; AMPM's existing hotel data and each family's guest list arrive as spreadsheets.

nodes.label: Authentication: client sign-in, staff second factor, password reset
nodes.rationale: GP-31: 'secure authentication' was unspecified; all three were defined (A-13, Q13), with no self-registration route anywhere.

nodes.label: Function readiness calculated from the checklist, separate from function status
nodes.rationale: AM-3: readiness and a function's own status (planned, confirmed, cancelled) are different things; both are kept and readiness is calculated from the checklist (A-26). Readiness cannot complete without required checks or an authorised exception.

nodes.label: Nine areas on desktop, five tabs on phones
nodes.rationale: CF-3: nine areas in the specification, five tabs in the flowchart with Hotels and Guests absent; the redrawn team app keeps the five tabs on phones and shows the nine areas on desktop (W-2). 'Database' under More is read as the hotel database (AM-6).

nodes.label: Proposed retention and deletion periods
nodes.rationale: GP-44: retention and deletion rules are left to AMPM; periods were proposed so the design could include the deletion jobs (A-17, Q17).

nodes.label: Rupees, English and Indian time; guest portal ready for a second language
nodes.rationale: Q16/A-16: 'Indian wedding destinations' is the only place the market is named.

nodes.label: No external hotel system integration in the first release
nodes.rationale: GP-39: 'external hotel systems' is not defined anywhere; the boundary is documented as manual.

nodes.label: Built for AMPM alone, not for licensing to other planners
nodes.rationale: AM-14: 'a paid business asset' could hint at licensing the software to other planners; one structural change is cheaper now than later if that is a real intention (A-30).

nodes.label: Responsive website installable like an app
nodes.rationale: Q1/GP-33: the specification asks for a responsive website while the flowcharts and briefs say 'app'; a responsive website that installs like an app was designed, native apps being a separate choice with a cost.

nodes.label: Share action and preview-as-client on every shareable record
nodes.rationale: Every record that can be shared has a share action the team controls and a preview that shows exactly what the client will see.

hyperedges.label: AMPM's five source documents reviewed by the audit
Four connected experiences plus demo mode of one shared platform
